title: Rav Shmuel Kaputka’a
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Chullin 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.27b.10), where he said: “You can know this, for birds have scales on their legs like fish.” [Kohelet Rabbah 7:23](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.7.23.3) cites the saying, with Rabbi Avin speaking in his name.[^1]
And in [Jerusalem Talmud Challah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Challah.3.1.7), Rabbi Yona [reports something] in his name.

He is also mentioned without the title "Rabbi" in [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 6:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.6.5.4), and [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 6:6 (Hyman cites 6:5)](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.6.6.7).
And Rabbi Chagai was his groomsman [shoshvin], as in [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.6.5).

notes.text: The linked Kohelet Rabbah, numbered 7:23 in this edition beside Hyman’s 4:23, gives Rabbi Avin speaking in Rabbi Shmuel’s name about chicken feet and fish scales. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3390&lang=en) points to the same verse. The linked Challah names Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Shmuel but leaves the link between them implicit. The linked Berakhot has Rabbi Chagai call himself Rabbi Shmuel’s shoshvin.
